gloss: to blow away; to blow off; to dispel

definitions.gloss: to blow away; to blow off
definitions.explanation: To cause something to fly away by blowing.
Figuratively, to get rid of negative feelings or atmosphere.

definitions.gloss: to blow wide open; to blast
definitions.explanation: To destroy or break something apart with force.

examples.japanese: {強風|きょうふう}が{屋根|やね}を{吹|ふ}き{飛|と}ばした。
examples.english: The strong wind blew off the roof.

examples.japanese: {憂|ゆう}うつな{気分|きぶん}を{吹|ふ}き{飛|と}ばそう。
examples.english: Let's blow away this gloomy feeling.

examples.japanese: {爆発|ばくはつ}で{建物|たてもの}の{一部|いちぶ}が{吹|ふ}き{飛|と}ばされた。
examples.english: Part of the building was blown apart by the explosion.

notes:
{吹|ふ}き{飛|と}ばす is a transitive verb ({他動詞|たどうし}). The intransitive form is {吹|ふ}き{飛|と}ぶ (to be blown away).

ASPECT ({ている}):
{吹|ふ}き{飛|と}ばしている indicates an ongoing action of blowing something away.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {風|かぜ}が[noun]を{吹|ふ}き{飛|と}ばす - wind blows [noun] away
- {悩|なや}み/{ストレス}を{吹|ふ}き{飛|と}ばす - to blow away worries/stress
- {眠気|ねむけ}を{吹|ふ}き{飛|と}ばす - to shake off sleepiness

COMPOUND VERB STRUCTURE:
{吹|ふ}く (to blow) + {飛|と}ばす (to make fly) = {吹|ふ}き{飛|と}ばす

FIGURATIVE USE:
Commonly used to describe getting rid of negative emotions or states, especially in the phrase [feeling]を{吹|ふ}き{飛|と}ばす.
